notes: Account snapshot: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Building an assistant inside product + relevance/rerank for search. Heavy focus on latency for in-app prompts (p95 target <= 200ms) and predictable monthly spend.
Initial onboarding: started on Hosted API (Dec 2025) using free credits. Quick POC: 2-week pilot of chat + reranking endpoints; integrated embeddings for search vector store.
POC outputs: Hosted API satisfied quality, but token costs and 2nd-region latency spikes prompted Dedicated evaluation.
Customer quote (from VP Product): 'we need consistent tail latency and a predictable bill — can't have bursts nuking MRR margins.'
Dedicated ask: reserved vGPU pool to guarantee sub-200ms p95 for in-product assistant; support for canary rollouts and auto-fallback to hosted in rare outage; SSO + audit log retention 12 months.
Model preferences: open models first (ggml/llama-style) for cost; willing to test Redwood-verified model variants. Interested in quantized profile suggestions from Optimize.
Traffic profile: peak user flows 9am-11am PT; expected steady-state 60k messages/day at launch; growth ramp to ~250k messages/day in 9 months.
Latency/throughput targets: p95 <= 200ms for chat assistant; sustained throughput >= 600 reqs/min per model route; embedding batch throughput 20k vectors/hour.
POC notes: Hosted p95 = 150ms from east coast; occasional p95 spikes to 800ms when throttled. Dedicated demo with 2xA10 equiv showed consistent p95 ~120ms for 1k concurrent sessions.

Pricing conversation: initial Redwood quote (Dedicated): $22k/month reserve for 2xA10 equiv with 3-month ramp, burst allowance 2x baseline for short windows, overage rate 1.5x per unit. Silvermarsh pushing for lower overage or blended rate.

Packaged asks from customer: 1) 3-month ramp schedule with step-up commit (month1 40%, month2 70%, month3 100%), 2) defined burst pool (2x baseline, 100 GPU-hours/month) included, 3) clearer definition of overage billing (tokens vs GPU-hours), 4) SLA 99.9 with credits.

Finance feedback: procurement wants annual commit option (12 months) to get 18% discount; prefers commit tied to GPU-hour baseline not token counts. Wants cap on monthly overage charges (ceiling at 25% over commit) for first year.
Security checklist: SSO (SAML) in place in staging; need SOC2 attestation + audit log ingestion into their Splunk; legal asks for data residency clause for EU customers.
Internal Redwood notes: SE demo ran model variant xg-3-median; Optimize recommended KV-caching on first 2 tokens to reduce steady-state cost by ~12% for their prompt pattern.
Risk: multi-region failover experiment required; customer will need a fallback policy to hosted API if Dedicated region degraded. They want runbooks and an RTO < 15 minutes for failover.
Sales play: propose a 9-month ramp + annual billing for committed capacity; include one-time migration assistance credit and 2-week post-launch SRE support window.

Decision criteria (from VP Eng): predictable spend, latency SLOs, turnkey deployment for canary rollouts, and strong audit/KMS integration. If Redwood meets commit/overage terms they will replace internal inference stack.
Current blocker summary: legal wants explicit data residency language, finance pushing for lower overage multiplier, product ops wants validation of burst behavior under load.

Next meeting: pricing call w/finance + legal (Mar 18). Action items: update SOW with ramp table, provide sample billing calc for token vs GPU-hour model, clarify overage ceilings and burst pool sizing.
